summary: Contestants create a 1-2 minute informational video explaining how AI is used in everyday life and how individuals can responsibly interact with emerging technologies. The video is submitted online and presented to judges, who evaluate both the technical quality and the contestant's presentation. The target audience is middle school and high school students beginning to interact with AI.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit all of the following in one combined PDF: Clickable URL to video, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted
The contestant is responsible for securing a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including oneself, whose image or work is used in the project
The contestant is responsible for citing all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Students may use one single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Apply user-centered design principles & elements analysis to create, manage, and distribute digital media content - including graphics, audio, video, and interactive elements - for a target audience, tailored to specific demographics, needs, and behaviors across web, social, and mobile platforms.

Utilize industry-standard software applications (such as Adobe Creative Cloud, video editing suites, and web development tools) and integrate graphic design principles with multimedia elements—color, animation, audio, and video—to produce engaging, accessible, and brand-consistent digital experiences.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Contestant submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing clickable URL to Project, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: The video exhibits outstanding clarity, sharpness, and precise focus throughout—enhancing visual engagement and presenting content with professional-level quality.
Thoughtful and intentional framing enhances the message with strong visual impact; composition is balanced and aesthetically engaging throughout.
Audio quality is professional-grade—exceptionally clear, balanced, and crisp, with no detectable distractions; elevates the listening experience and enhances engagement.
Dialogue or voice-over is crystal clear, well-paced, and delivered with ideal volume and tone; enhances comprehension and reinforces the message with professional polish.
Editing is polished and purposeful, with creative cuts and transitions that enhance the story, rhythm, and viewer experience.
Transitions are well-timed and thoughtfully placed, enhancing storytelling and creating a smooth, unified visual flow.
Graphics are well-designed and strategically used—clear, integrated text enhances understanding and elevates the viewer’s experience, with every element supporting the message.
Lighting is expertly balanced and purposefully enhances the subject. It adds depth, clarity, and mood that elevate the video’s quality and viewer engagement.
The content delivers a strong and engaging message, using creativity and emotional appeal to effectively appeal to the audience.
The video makes strategic use of its full time—content is well-structured, purposeful, and engaging.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
The presentation content flows adequately, and the contestant demonstrates a clear and well-integrated structure throughout.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event
Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
